title: Accountant Document Chaser
summary: Accountants waste hours every week chasing clients for missing receipts. The bot finds what's missing and chases the client automatically.
hook: "Hi, can you please send the March receipts? … Hi again, just a reminder about March… Hi, still missing March…"
story:
**Emma runs a small accounting firm with 4 people and 90 client companies.** Every month, before she can close the books, she needs every receipt and invoice from every client. But clients are busy: a restaurant owner forgets, a plumber sends a blurry photo, a shop owner sends the wrong month.

Her team spends **hours every week** writing reminder emails, checking which transaction has no receipt and calling clients. That time is mostly **not billable**. Month-end gets delayed, VAT filings get stressful, and everyone is annoyed.

whyReal.title: Every accountant has it
whyReal.text: Chasing clients for paperwork is one of the most common complaints in accounting communities. Some accountants describe spending half their week on reminders.

whyReal.title: It costs them money
whyReal.text: Chasing time is usually unbilled. It's either written off or causes fights over the bill.

whyReal.title: It repeats every month
whyReal.text: It's not a one-time problem. Every client, every month, so the tool is used constantly.

whyReal.title: Concentrated buyers
whyReal.text: One accounting firm brings 30–200 client companies. One sale means many paying seats.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: one country and one accounting software first (e.g. Xero or QuickBooks for English-speaking markets, Fortnox in Sweden, SmartBill/Saga in Romania), then expand.

solution.title: Connect
solution.text: the firm connects its accounting software (Xero / QuickBooks / Fortnox API) in one click.

solution.title: Detect
solution.text: every day the bot checks bank transactions and finds the ones with **no receipt or invoice attached**.

solution.title: Chase
solution.text: it sends the client a friendly SMS or email in the firm's name: "Hi James, we're missing the receipt for €84.20 at Shell on 12 March. Tap here to upload."

solution.title: Upload
solution.text: the client taps the link, takes a photo and it's done. No login, no app.

solution.title: Match
solution.text: AI reads the receipt (OCR), checks it matches the transaction and attaches it automatically.

solution.title: Escalate
solution.text: if the client ignores 3 reminders, the accountant gets an alert. The dashboard shows each client's status (complete / missing 4 / ignoring).

timeline.what: **Concierge pilot.** 2 accounting firms export their missing-receipt list, we send the reminders manually, and we measure how many get resolved.
Accounting API integration, missing-document detection, reminder engine.
Pilot firms switch to paid; Jonatan signs the next 5 firms.

pricing.name: Free 30-day pilot
pricing.description: We show the hours saved, then they pay

competitors.name: Dext, Hubdoc
competitors.gap: Client must remember to upload; no proactive chasing

competitors.name: Content Snare, TaxDome, Karbon
competitors.gap: Big, English/US-focused, not tied to "which bank transaction is missing a receipt"

competitors.name: Accounting software reminders
competitors.gap: Generic, not personalised, no SMS, no auto-matching

competitors.name: Us
competitors.what: Detect missing → chase by SMS → auto-match
competitors.gap: Fully automatic, works in the firm's name and language

risks.answer: Start with the software that has the easiest public API (Xero / QuickBooks).
Free pilot, results in 2 weeks, no change to their workflow.
Move fast, go deeper on chasing and on local markets.
EU hosting, data processing agreement, read-only access.

questions: How many hours a month does your team spend chasing clients for documents?
How do you chase today: email, phone, software reminders?
How much of that time can you bill?
Would you let a tool text your clients in your firm's name?
Which accounting software do you and your clients use?
